Exploit the n-scaled factor tolerance (rtol=20*n*eps32) to run GEMM-heavy trailing updates on tensor cores at reduced precision in Triton. Blocked Householder QR where panel factorization, reflectors and tau stay FP32, but the larfb-style trailing update V*(T^T*(V^T*A)) runs via tl.dot in TF32/FP16 with FP32 accumulate; re-orthogonalize if needed to hold the 100*n*eps32 orthogonality gate. Verify rankdef/nearrank/nearcollinear/clustered still pass. Emit packed (H,tau).
Blocked Householder QR, closed-form WY T-factor, FP32 trailing update (b=64). 1.489x geomean. Panel geqrf dominates (75% GPU time); trailing GEMM tiny so TF32 there is moot and breaks factor gate.
Per-n config: blocked b=64 for n in {176,352,512,1024} (n=176/352 beat geqrf ~3x), TF32 b=256 for n in {2048,4096} (n-scaled tol absorbs TF32 error). n=32->geqrf. 1.534x geomean.

Hybrid panel factorization: manual batched unblocked Householder for tall panels (m>256, dodges geqrf domino cliff, ~9-18x faster), geqrf for short panels. Per-n tuned b (16/32). n>=2048 geqrf-blocked. 3.82x geomean (30274).

BEST: 3.82x geomean (30274 us vs 115731 baseline), commit 9872f7b9, validates fully (22 shapes + 3 guards). Brief was reduced-precision trailing updates; KEY FINDING is that the trailing update is NOT the bottleneck (it's 2-8% of time for n<=1024, panel factorization is 73-98%), so TF32 trailing gives ~0 speedup AND breaks the factor gate at n=512 (scaled 25-30>20). TF32 trailing only helps at n>=2048 (n-scaled tol absorbs error, GEMM big enough to be compute-bound) -- applied there for +2-5%. The BIG win came from a discovered torch.geqrf cliff: cuSOLVER switches to a ~33x-slower geqr2_smem_domino kernel at panel height m>256. A manual batched UNBLOCKED Householder QR (rank-1 GEMV updates, no cuSOLVER) dodges it and is 9-18x faster on tall panels; geqrf's fast batched path keeps m<=256 panels. Blocked QR (b=16/32 per n) with closed-form compact-WY T=inv(diag(1/tau)+triu(V^T V,1)) for the FP32 trailing update. Per-shape: n=512 18x, n=176 6x, n=352 2x, n=1024 1.86x, n=2048/4096 ~1.0-1.05x (geqrf-blocked, manual is launch-bound there at small batch). PLATEAU: remaining cost is the manual panel's per-column launch overhead (~10 small kernels/column) -- profile shows geqr2_smem_domino is gone, replaced by many small elementwise/norm/where launches. NEXT DIRECTION: a fused Triton panel kernel (one launch per panel, sequential reflectors in shared memory) to kill that overhead -- this is worker-0's brief, so I did not duplicate it. Also n=2048/4096 (small batch, large n) have no good PyTorch path and need Triton. torch.compile and inner-blocking the panel did NOT help. The closed-form WY T-factor and the manual-HH panel are reusable building blocks for a combine.

Extend the fused Triton blocked-Householder kernel (global best, currently n=512/1024) to the remaining geqrf-fallback shapes, biggest proven win first. SECONDARY n=2048 (batch8): Worker 1 verified the fused kernel does ~1.2x as-is at B=32 VT=128 -- add it. Keep n=4096 (batch2) on torch.geqrf (verified 25x slower, only 2 CTAs). Do not regress any shape. Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN.

Tuned n=352 to B=16/RT=32/CT=32 (910us, 41x; was 1070us/35x). n=2048 sweep confirmed B=32/VT=128 optimal at 1.20x (occupancy-bound, batch=8). All tests+guards CLEAN. Geomean 8637 (parent/trial 1.375x, baseline 13.4x).

Tuned B=16/RT=32/CT=32/VT=512 (structured sweep; B=16 fits the 352-wide matrix better than B=32). This branch is combine-ready: it's a clean superset of the global best (parent kernels untouched, +n=352/+n=2048 coverage).

Attack the two largest remaining log-space terms, both small-batch large-n still slow: n=4096 (batch2, ~48ms, on geqrf) and n=2048 (batch8, ~61ms, fused only 1.20x). Both starve the one-CTA-per-matrix panel factor (2-8 CTAs on 188 SMs). geqrf at n=4096 runs only ~5 TFLOPS (far below ~125 peak) => NOT compute-bound, real headroom. Pursue MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX panel factorization: split each matrix's tall panel across CTAs (row-block norm reductions, two-pass) to manufacture enough CTAs to fill the GPU from tiny batch -- this is the OPPOSITE regime from the n=512/1024 smem-reduction ceiling (Worker 0 proved TSQR can't help THAT, but here the problem is too-few-CTAs, not too-many). Use TF32 tensor-core trailing (you proved it's safe at n>=2048 under the n-scaled tolerance). Keep multi-CTA col-tile trailing. Add n=4096 to the grid only if it beats geqrf; don't regress. The brief framed it as occupancy starvation needing multi-CTA panels, but the REAL cause was REGISTER SPILL: the fused panel-factor keeps the [n,B] panel resident per CTA, and at n=2048/B=32 the tall [2048,32] panel = 255 regs/thread spills to local mem (ncu: 16.6% occupancy). Halving to B=16 ([2048,16]) -> 22 regs/thread, 88% occupancy (ncu-confirmed) -> 4.24x. RT=CT=32. Also restored n=352 B=16 (910us; the combine had reset it to B=32). n=512/1024 untouched (no regression). MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX PANEL = CONFIRMED DEAD END for n=4096 (real attempt + hard evidence): (1) the one-CTA [4096,B] panel spills catastrophically regardless of B/warps -- best 0.34x at B=16/nwpf=32 (147ms vs geqrf 50ms); (2) a multi-CTA TSQR LEAF is 46x faster (187us vs 8729us/panel, no spill) BUT produces row-block-local reflectors, and emitting CANONICAL packed (H,tau) requires a sequential per-column resident reconstruction that worker-0 independently proved has the identical bottleneck; (3) per-column two-pass via separate launches costs 4.83us/launch x 2n = 39.5ms launch overhead alone for n=4096; (4) Triton has no grid-wide sync for a single-kernel multi-CTA panel; (5) CholeskyQR-based reconstruction numerically FAILS at n=4096 FP32 (A^T A not positive-definite). So n=4096 stays on geqrf (unbeatable here). TF32 trailing for n=2048 rejected: only +1.7% (trailing is 8% of time) and pushes rankdef/nearrank sfr to 15.6 (gate 20) -- too risky; FP32 ieee trailing keeps sfr 0.013. KEY GENERALIZABLE INSIGHT for the fleet: the B=32 default register-spills on ANY tall small-batch panel -- worth checking B=16 on any other spill-bound shape. This branch is a clean superset of the global best (only _CFG changes); combine-ready.
